Definition: , also (separately) οὐκ ἔτι from G3756 and G2089; not yet, no longer:--after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter) not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not).
BiblicalUsage: No longer, or no more, marks what has ended. When Philip was caught away, the eunuch saw him no more, and went on his way rejoicing, and Paul said he called God for a record that to spare the Corinthians he came not as yet unto Corinth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no longer is the word of a changed life: the eunuch saw Philip no more, and Paul would not come to Corinth again in heaviness — some things end, and that is grace.
